subject.title: Android: add adaptive app navigation sidebar

question: After final-head device or emulator proof confirms the compact, rail, and drawer layouts, should OpenClaw adopt this Material 3 adaptive-navigation replacement as the Android shell baseline?
rationale: The patch replaces a core Android interaction model across form factors, so adequate behavior proof can establish correctness but cannot by itself determine whether the new navigation baseline is the intended product direction.

options.title: Accept the adaptive baseline after proof
options.body: Merge once final-head evidence shows the requested layouts and compact-state behavior without regressions.

options.title: Narrow the replacement
options.body: Keep the existing shell and land only a smaller, explicitly scoped navigation improvement if the full adaptive rework is not desired.

options.title: Pause for Android UX direction
options.body: Hold the PR until an Android owner documents the intended navigation model for phones, tablets, and foldables.

recommendation.title: Accept the adaptive baseline after proof
recommendation.body: Merge once final-head evidence shows the requested layouts and compact-state behavior without regressions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent review activity is the only supplied concrete maintainer signal tied to the remaining Android proof and UX decision.
